themes.name: Judgment That Won't Compile
themes.plain: The hardest calls are about meaning, not data: whether a headline next to a picture implies a promise, whether evidence really backs a claim, whether two teams can both be right about what "customer" means. Today all three models said the same thing about disputed definitions: a shared layer can expose and version the disagreement, but it cannot settle a fight that has budget attached.
themes.evidence: On the governed semantic context layer, all three models called conflicting definitions an organizational power struggle rather than a modeling gap, and on governance of generative content at volume all three said implied meaning and context resist automated checking.

themes.name: No Ground Truth to Measure Against
themes.plain: Most of these problems have no answer key. There is no trustworthy record of who is really the same person, what an AI assistant would have said anyway, or what sales would have been without the ad, so the models start by building or buying a small truth set they can grade themselves against.
themes.evidence: Answer engine optimization, cross-channel incrementality, durable identity resolution, and loss of B2B buying-group signal all drew first moves built around panels, holdouts, and labeled sets created before any model is built.

themes.name: Chokepoint Before Trust
themes.plain: When the models cannot trust who is acting or what happens next, they build one door they own and push everything through it. A sent email, a spent dollar, or an exported list cannot be called back, so the only real control happens before the action leaves.
themes.evidence: Safe agent execution drew proxies and gateways in front of every write, downstream consent enforcement drew a single egress gate, journey orchestration drew one shared contact log with veto power, and today's semantic layer answers routed agents through warehouse-defined endpoints instead of letting them read tools directly.

themes.name: Nobody Can Verify Downstream
themes.plain: Once data, a message, or a dollar leaves your own systems, you cannot see inside the partner, ad platform, or trained model that now holds it. The best anyone offers is watching from outside: planting fake records and seeing what comes back, or expiring every list you send so nothing lives on by default.
themes.evidence: Downstream consent and deletion answers converged on canary profiles and short-lived audiences because trained models and walled gardens allow no read-back, and identity resolution and ad supply integrity hit the same wall of closed platforms.

themes.name: Incentives Before Standards
themes.plain: Many of these problems stall because whoever holds the answer gains nothing by sharing it, and nobody can force them. So the models try to make honesty pay, or they stop waiting for cooperation and work with only what they already own.
themes.evidence: On governing agentic traffic the models proposed fast lanes and discounts for agents that declare themselves, while incrementality, journey orchestration, and ad supply integrity each named a party that profits from the current fog.
